title.source: Section check: Trade, power and everyday lives
title.back: Section check: Trade, power and everyday life

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 4–6. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 4–6. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.options.0.text.source: Many buyers try to buy the same spice.
questions.0.options.0.text.back: Many buyers try to buy the same spice.

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. When many buyers can compete, no one has a monopoly. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. When many buyers can compete, no one has a monopoly. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: One buyer shuts all the others out.
questions.0.options.1.text.back: One buyer keeps out all other buyers.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The VOC wanted to be the only buyer of Banda's nutmeg, so no one else could compete.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.note: VOC is explained once as บริษัทอินเดียตะวันออกของดัตช์, as KEY_TERMS asks for the first time it appears. Second pass: nutmeg is ลูกจันทน์เทศ (SAT04's glossary word) here and in the course text, which said จันทน์เทศ.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The VOC (the Dutch East India Company) wanted to be the only buyer of Banda's nutmeg, so no one could compete.

questions.0.options.2.text.back: Traders exchange goods without using money.

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Swapping goods is a kind of trade. A monopoly is when one group shuts other buyers or sellers out. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Exchanging goods is one kind of trade. A monopoly is when one group keeps other buyers or sellers out. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.1.question.source: The painting of Banda Neira cannot tell the whole story. Why not?
questions.1.question.note: Banda Neira is บันดาเนรา. "cannot tell the whole story" is เล่าเรื่องได้ไม่ครบทั้งหมด.
questions.1.question.back: The painting of Banda Neira does not tell the whole story. Why?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: It was made for the VOC, much later
questions.1.options.0.text.back: It was painted for the VOC a long time afterwards.

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The VOC paid for it more than 40 years after 1621. It shows the company's view, not what Bandanese people lived through.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.note: "what Bandanese people lived through" is สิ่งที่ชาวบันดาต้องเผชิญ. The 1621 events on Banda were violent (a massacre and forced removal by the VOC); the English is understated on purpose and the Thai keeps that tone. Sensitive history: check the tone matches SAT04.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The VOC paid for this painting more than 40 years after 1621. It shows the company's point of view, not what the Bandanese went through.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: It was painted before nutmeg grew there
questions.1.options.1.text.back: It was painted before nutmeg trees grew there.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Nutmeg grew on Banda for hundreds of years before the painting. It shows rows of nutmeg trees. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Nutmeg trees grew on Banda for hundreds of years before this picture. The picture has nutmeg trees in rows. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: A painting can never be used as evidence
questions.1.options.2.text.back: Paintings can never be used as evidence.

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The painting is useful evidence. It shows how the company chose to show Banda. It just cannot tell the whole story. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This painting is useful evidence. It shows how the company chose to present Banda; it just does not tell the whole story. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.2.question.source: Rubber went from a tree to a buyer far away. Which work did workers do on the way?
questions.2.question.back: Rubber travelled from the tree to a faraway buyer. Along the way, what work did workers do?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: Buying shares in a rubber company

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. An investor bought shares, hoping to get more money back. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.note: investor is นักลงทุน. Second pass: checked, it is SAT05's glossary word; flag removed.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Investors bought shares, hoping to get more money back. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: Choosing photos for a souvenir book
questions.2.options.1.text.back: Choose photos for a souvenir book

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The book's makers chose the photos. Workers tapped trees and collected and carried the rubber. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The book's makers chose the photos. Workers tapped rubber trees, collected latex and carried rubber. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.2.options.2.text.note: "Tapping trees and collecting latex" is กรีดต้นยางและเก็บน้ำยาง: กรีดยาง is the everyday Thai word; latex (SAT05 glossary) is น้ำยาง.
questions.2.options.2.text.back: Tap rubber trees and collect latex

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Workers tapped each tree and collected the latex. Others made it into sheets and took it to ships.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. Workers tapped rubber trees one by one and collected latex. Another group of workers made the latex into sheets, then took them to ships.

questions.3.stimulus.title.source: A made-up postcard from a made-up tea estate
questions.3.stimulus.title.back: A made-up postcard from a made-up tea estate

questions.3.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A postcard from 1925 shows a tea estate on the made-up hill of Tavin. Rows of tea bushes cover the hill. Two workers pick leaves into baskets. A shop sold the postcard to visitors.
questions.3.stimulus.body.note: estate (SAT05 glossary) is ไร่ here (ไร่ชา, tea estate); a rubber estate would be สวนยาง. Check against the lesson's chosen word. Second pass: SAT05's glossary word for estate is สวนขนาดใหญ่; ไร่ชา is kept here because it is the everyday Thai for a tea estate and the question does not test the word.
questions.3.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A postcard from 1925 shows a tea estate on a made-up hillside called Tavin. Rows of tea bushes fill the hill. Two workers are picking tea leaves into baskets. A shop sold this postcard to tourists.

questions.3.question.source: Which source could tell you what these workers were paid?
questions.3.question.back: Which source could tell you how much these workers were paid?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: A bigger copy of the same postcard

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A bigger copy shows the same scene. A picture cannot show pay. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A bigger picture still shows the same scene. It cannot show wages. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: A pay record from the estate
questions.3.options.1.text.back: The wage records of this tea estate

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Pay is written in records, or told by the workers. A postcard shows only what its makers chose.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. Wages are written in records, or the workers tell them. A postcard shows only what its makers chose to show.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: The number of baskets in the picture
questions.3.options.2.text.back: The number of baskets in the picture

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The baskets show the work, not the pay. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Baskets show work, not wages. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.4.question.source: In 1903, Kartini and her sister were offered a scholarship. What happened next?
questions.4.question.note: Kartini's sister Roekmini was younger, so น้องสาว (Thai must say older or younger). "were offered a scholarship" is ได้รับการเสนอทุนการศึกษา, slightly stiff.
questions.4.question.back: In 1903, Kartini and her sister were offered a scholarship. What happened after that?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: The sisters did not use the money.
questions.4.options.0.text.back: The two sisters did not use the money.

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A decision shows what officials agreed to. It does not show what happened next. The sisters did not use the money.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.note: "A decision" (the colonial government's decision of 7 July 1903) is การตัดสินใจของรัฐบาล. คำตัดสิน sounds like a court ruling; มติ is another option. Same word in questions.5.options.1.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The government's decision shows what officials agreed, but not what happened later. The two sisters did not use the money.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Kartini used it to study in Batavia.
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Kartini used the scholarship to study in Batavia.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The money was offered for study in Batavia. But the sisters did not use it. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The money was offered for study in Batavia, but the two sisters did not use it. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: Kartini used it to open her school.
questions.4.options.2.text.back: Kartini used the scholarship to open her school.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The school was a hope in her 1901 letter. The scholarship was a different thing, and it was not used. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The school was a hope in her 1901 letter. The scholarship is a different matter, and it was not used. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.5.question.source: You read Kartini's 1901 letter in an English book from 1921. Which question is good to ask about it?
questions.5.question.back: You read Kartini's 1901 letter in an English book from 1921. Which is a good question to ask about this letter?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Why did Kartini write it in English?
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Why did Kartini write in English?

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Kartini wrote mostly in Dutch. The English words are a translation. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Kartini wrote mostly in Dutch. The English words are a translation. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The letter is from 1901, and it tells us a hope. The decision is a different source. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. This letter is from 1901 and tells of her hopes. The government's decision is a different source. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Who chose and translated the letters?
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Who chose and translated these letters?

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. An editor chose which letters to print, and the book has only some of them. A translator made choices too.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.note: "A translator made choices too" is ผู้แปลก็เลือกหลายอย่างเช่นกัน.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. An editor chose which letters to print, and the book has only some letters. The translator made many choices too.

results.high.source: Well done. You asked who made each source, and whose story it leaves out.
results.high.back: Great work. You asked who made each source and whose story was left out.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Well done. You got many right. Go back to the lessons for the questions you have not got right yet, then try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 4–6, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 4–6 and try again. Take as long as you need.
